questions.question: Which of the following places in India has 0% forest area as per the Indian State of Forest Report 2019?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lakshadweep.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indian State of Forest Report 2019**__

 
 
• India **State of Forest Report 2019** is the **16th biennial assessment of India's** forests by the **Forest Survey of India.**
 
• **FSI **undertakes the **National Forest inventory to assess the growing stock in forests and TOF, bamboo resource, carbon stock and to assess the dependence of the people living in Forest Fringe Villages for fuelwood, fodder, small timber, and bamboo.**
 
• The 2019 report for the first time has assessed the qualitative nature of the forest cover, including listing its biodiversity and the type of plants and trees found.
 
• It also created a national forest inventory for the first time on produce from forests.
 
• **Forest Cover (ARea wise)** : Madhya Pradesh> Arunachal Pradesh> Chhattisgarh> Odisha> Maharashtra.
 
• **Forest Cover (Percentage)**: Mizoram (85.4%)> Aruncachal Pradesh(79.63%)> Meghalaya (76.33%).

questions.question: Which of the following states/union territories is NOT touched by the Aravalli Range?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Aravalli Range is a mountain range in Northwestern India, the length of the range is approximately 692 km in a southwest direction.
 
• The Aravalli range starts from Delhi, passing through southern Haryana and Rajasthan, and ending in Gujarat.
 
• Hence, it does not pass through Punjab.
 
• The literal meaning of the Aravalli Range is **‘line of peaks’.**

 [IMAGE: https://www.learncbse.in/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Class-11-Geography-NCERT-Solutions-Chapter-2-Structure-and-Physiography-Map-Skills-Q1.1.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The highest peak is Guru Shikhar at 1,722 meters (5,650 ft) situated in Mount Abu.
 
• The Aravalli Range is the oldest range of fold mountains in India.
 
• The Aravalli Range is very rich in natural resources and gave rise to numerous peninsula rivers like **Banas, Luni, Sakhi, and Sabarmati.**
 
• This region is also famous for heavily forested consisting of large areas of sand and stone and of masses of rose-colored quartzite.

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest mangrove forest in the world?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sundarbans Reserve Forest.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• World’s largest deltaic mangrove forests are found in Sundarbans Reserve Forest.__
 
• The Sundarbans Reserve Forest is located in **both India and Bangladesh**, and is part of the Ganges Delta.
 
• It lies on the delta of Meghna, Brahmaputra, and Ganges rivers.
 
• It is known for its wide range of fauna, comprising 260 bird species.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Mangrove, any of certain shrubs and trees that grow in dense bushes or forests along tidal estuaries, in salt marshes, and on muddy coasts.
 
• Mangroves serve as a** buffer between marine and terrestrial ecosystems **and protect shorelines from damaging winds, waves, and floods.
 
• India has a total mangrove cover of 4,975 sq km.
 
• It is 0.15% of the country’s total geographical area.
 
• West Bengal has 42.45% of India’s mangrove cover.
 
• West Bengal is followed by Gujarat at 23.66% and Andaman & Nicobar Islands at 12.39%. 
 
• Sundarban Mangroves are found in West Bengal.

questions.question: Which Indian state is divided into Majha, Doaba and Malwa regions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab**__.

__
 
• **Punjab** is a state in the northwest region of India and is one of the most prosperous states.

 
 
• The name Punjab is made of two words Punj (Five) + Aab (Water) i.e. land of five rivers.
 
• These five rivers of Punjab are **Sutlej, Beas, Ravi, Chenab, and Jhelum**. Only Sutlej, Ravi and Beas rivers flow in today’s Punjab.
 
• The other two rivers are now in the state of Punjab, situated in Pakistan.
 
• **The Punjab State is divided into three regions: Majha, Doaba and Malwa**__.

questions.question: A channel of a canal, where water is carried by force uplift in the opposite direction of the slope of the land, is called _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** lift Channel.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A channel of a canal, where water is carried by force uplift in the opposite direction of the slope of the land, is called** hoisting system.**
 
• When the main source is at a lower level than the supply level. Then water is supplied through some mechanical means. This is known as lift irrigation.
 
• Lift irrigation is a method of irrigation in which water instead of being transported by natural flow (as in gravity-fed canal systems) requires external energy through fuel-based, or electric power using pumps or other mechanical means.
 
• The left channel method is used both for watering of a certain area as a whole and for water application to particular elevated sites in the area of gravity irrigation, For example, water is lifted from rivers or from irrigation canals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **An aquifer** is a body of rock and/or sediment that holds groundwater.

 
 
• Groundwater is the word used to describe precipitation that has infiltrated the soil beyond the surface and collected in empty spaces underground. 
 
 
 
• **Drainage** is the natural or artificial removal of a surface's water and sub-surface water from an area with excess of water. 
 
• **The command area** is the area around the dam/ project, where the area gets benefits from the dam, such as irrigation water, electricity, etc.

questions.question: The two streams Chandra and Bhaga rise on the opposite sides of the Baralacha pass to form which of the following rivers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chenab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Chenab originates from near the** Bara Lacha Pass **in the **Lahul-Spiti part of the Zaskar Range**.
 
• The two streams, the **Chandra and the Bhaga** join at **Tandi in Himachal Pradesh** forming the Chenab river (also known as the Chandrabhaga river).
 
• It is traditionally known as the **Chandrabhaga River**, which is a major river that flows in **India and Pakistan**.
 
• It is the largest tributary of the **Indus river**.
 
• Its important tributaries are the **Marusadar River, Miyar Nalla, Sohal and Thirot**.
 
• Major dam on the Chenab river is **Pakal Dul Dam, Dul Hasti Hydroelectric Plant, Baglihar Hydroelectric power project and Salal Dam**.
 
• The **world's highest rail bridge** is formed above the Chenab river.

questions.question: In which of the following Indian states will you find the Netarhat Mountains, also called 'Queen of Chotanagpur'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jharkhand.**__

__
 
• **Netarhat mountains** are found in a town in Latehar district, Jharkhand.
 
• Referred to as the "Queen of Chotanagpur", it is a hill station.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Important hills in Jharkhand:**__

 
 
• Parasnath Hill is also recognized as Sri Sammed Sikharji.

 
 
• Parasnath Hill is situated in the Giridih district of Jharkhand. Hence, option 1 is correct.
 
• It is a chief Jain pilgrimage site and the holy place for Jains.
 
• It is believed in the Jain culture that 20 of the 24 Tirthankaras attained Moksha from this place.
 
 
 
• Rajmahal Hills are located in the Sahibganj and Godda districts of the Eastern part of Jharkhand.
 
 
• The Rajmahal hills belong to the Jurassic era.
 
• These hills like others also have many waterfalls, lakes, and greenery.
 
 
 
• Trikut Hill is located ten kilometers away from Deoghar and lies on the way to Dumka in Jharkhand.
 
• Tagore Hill is also recognized as **Morabadi Hill**.
 
 
• The Tagore hill is located in Morabadi, Ranchi.

questions.question: Which of the following is the main cause of 'bad lands'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Soil erosion.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Badlands** are a type of dry terrain where softer sedimentary rocks and clay-rich soils have been extensively eroded.
 
• Badlands are arid regions where the hills are badly eroded under the action of water due to occasional rainstorms or the flow of river streams.
 
• Gullies and ravines represent them.
 
• Badland is **rugged topography, usually of relatively low relief.**
 
• Badland is associated with the arid and semi-arid regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Types of Erosion are as follows

 
 
• Rain Drop Erosion - Due to falling raindrops on the soil surface.
 
• Sheet Erosion- Uniform removal of soil in thin layers from the surface.
 
• Rill Erosion - Erosion takes place through numerous narrow streamlets.
 
• Gully Erosion - Occurs due to runoff of surface water causing the removal of soil and forming gullies due to erosion.
 
• Stram Bank Erosion- Nothing but away from banks of a stream or a river.

questions.concept: Indian Rivers and Water Resources, Methods of Irrigation
questions.question: A channel of canal where water flows under the influence of gravity is called _______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**flow channel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Flow channel**

 
 
• These are also called **gravity irrigation**.
 
• **It is the type of irrigation in which water is available at a higher level to enable** **supply to the land by gravity flow. Hence, Option 4 is correct.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 
 
**Lift irrigation**

 
 
 
When groundwater is lifted up to be used as irrigation water or water supply is at too low a level to run by the gravitation of the land.

 
In this water is lifted up by some mechanical means such as a pump.

 
 
 

 
 
**Drip irrigation**

 
 
 
This is also called trickle irrigation as water is directly applied to the root zone of the plant using a drip nozzle.

 
In this method evaporation and percolation losses are very less.

 
This is the most efficient method.

 
 
 

 
 
**Sprinkler irrigation**

 
 
 
In this method of irrigation water is applied through a network of pipes and pumps. This method is suitable:

 
 
• when topography is irregular or rolling.
 
• when the water table is high 
 
• when water is not easily available 
 
• for more permeable as well as less permeable soil

questions.question: A salt-water lake separated from the sea by sandbars and spits is called a (an):
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**lagoon.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **lagoon is a small body of water** that is shielded from larger bodies of water by a sandbar or coral reef yet may have an **opening to them.**
 
• **Atoll lagoons and coastal lagoons **are two typical categories of lagoons. Many more names for lagoons include estuaries, sounds, bays, and **even lakes.**
 
• **Coastal lagoons are lagoons** that are protected by sandbars or barrier islands.
 
• The term "Lagoon" comes from the** Italian laguna, which describes **the waterways surrounding Venice and the** Lagoon of Venice.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A glacier is an enormous, enduring mass** of crystalline ice, snow, rock, silt, and frequently liquid water that originates on land and descends a slope under the weight of** itself and gravity. **
 
• A partially contained, coastal body of water called an estuary is where freshwater from rivers and streams and **saltwater from the ocean** mingle. **Estuaries and the regions **that surround them serve as transitional areas from the land to the sea.
 
• **A lake is a body of water** that is isolated from any rivers or other outlets that are used to fill or empty the lake, enclosed inside a basin, and **surrounded by land. **

questions.question: The northern most range of the Himalayan mountain is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Great Himalaya.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The northern most range of the Himalayan mountain is known as Great Himalaya.**
 
• It is also called Himadri.
 
• Himadri is the backbone of the Himalaya.
 
• It is the most continuous range consisting of the loftiest peaks with an average height of 6,000 metres.
 
• It contains all the prominent Himalayan peaks like Mount Everest, Annapoorna, Nandadevi, etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Himalaya is the youngest fold mountain range in the world.
 
• The word Himalaya means** "the abode of snow".**
 
• The Himalaya is mostly formed of sedimentary rocks.
 
• **The Himalayas consist of three main parallel ranges**, namely:
 
 
• The greater Himalayas.
 
• The lesser Himalayas.
 
• The outer Himalayas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3685eaf4c84e498288c4d5d7009f4f8038d31731b22cab9d43fa58463fd5a5c9.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Lesser Himalayas:**

 
 
• It is the mountain range that lies between Himadri and Siwalik.
 
• It is also called Himachal.
 
• It is mainly composed of highly compressed and altered rocks.
 
• The altitude varies between 3,700 and 4,500 metres and the average width is 50 Km.
 
• Pir Panjal is the largest range in Himachal.
 
• This region is well known for its hill stations.
 
 
 
• **The Shiwalik(Outer Himalayas):**
 
 
• The outermost range of the Himalayas is called the Shiwalik(Outer Himalayas.)
 
• It extends over a width of 10-50 Km and has an altitude varying between 900 and 1100 metres.
 
• The word Shiwalik literally means "tresses of Shiva".
 
• Shiwalik is parallel to the Ganga plain.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about black soil is INCORRECT?

options.text: It is found along the Deccan trap.
It is rich in phosphoric content.
It has a good capacity to hold moisture.
It develops deep cracks during hot weather.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**It is rich in phosphoric content**__.

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__**Properties of Black Soil**__

 
• It is found along the **Deccan trap**.
 
• It has a good capacity to **hold moisture**.
 
• It develops **deep cracks during hot weather.**
 
• It has rich in** calcium carbonate, magnesium, potash, and lime but poor in nitrogen and phosphorous.**
 
• It has a clayey texture and are highly fertile the structure of these soils is **cloddish or occasionally friable.**
 
• Ti is highly retentive of moisture, extremely compact and tenacious when wet contractible and develops deep wide cracks on drying.
 
• It has calcareous and neutral to mild alkaline in reaction, high in carbon exchange capacity and** low in organic matter.**
 
• It has property of self-ploughing and comparatively less fertile on the uplands than on the lowlands.
